findings.title: Adoption accepts unbound intermediate commits and hidden tracked paths
findings.reproduction: At candidate 060899b5ec438003ad188d3be21da1f29b8d3908, tools/gcrctl.py command_adopt checks only that --approved-state-commit equals HEAD^ and is ancestral to HEAD. It does not prove that this parent is the canonical commit applying the latest APPROVED ledger/state, does not constrain the reviewed-state-to-approved-state delta, and does not compare the complete approved-state-to-evidence-commit diff to the single canonical adoption-evidence path. A temporary real-Git replay subclassed the shipped happy-path lifecycle test so that planning/unauthorized-hidden.txt was added beside artifacts/evidence/governance-control-recovery/GCR-0001.B00.adoption.json in the evidence commit. The unchanged controller printed the 6-to-7 adoption success and the test passed with hidden_extra_commit_accepted=True. The shipped test inspects only the uncommitted post-command diff, so it cannot detect the already committed extra path. This violates the exact ancestry/path authority, hidden-extra-path denial, and direct-child adoption boundary required by acceptance criterion 8 and verification obligation 4.
findings.requiredRemediation: In a strict-descendant candidate, derive rather than trust the canonical latest reviewed-state and approved-state commits. Require the APPROVED ledger/state application to have the exact permitted status/path delta and ancestry, require the pre-adoption evidence commit to be its direct child with exactly one added canonical adoption-evidence file and no add/delete/rename/copy/type-change/substitution/omission/extra path, and verify that file's exact Git blob/hash. Add isolated real-Git denial tests for hidden paths and intermediate/substituted commits at both boundaries while preserving the append-only R01 finding and using fresh R02 evidence with an explicit closure.

findings.title: The two-file adoption writer is not interruption-atomic
findings.reproduction: tools/gcrctl.py atomic_adoption_write prepares two temporary files and then calls os.replace sequentially for planning/backlog.yaml and the canonical GCR state. Its exception handler can restore bytes only while the process remains alive. An independent child-process probe forced os._exit(77) immediately after the first real replacement; the child terminated with 77 and partial_write_observed=True: backlog bytes had advanced while GCR state bytes remained APPROVED. No durable transaction marker or startup recovery exists. Moreover, command_validate selects the revision from the backlog and validate_state_history accepts an APPROVED state with no adoption record, so the resulting revision-7/APPROVED split is not expressly rejected. The shipped affected suite has an exception-path atomic-save test for a different single-file writer but no abrupt-interruption GCR adoption test. This violates acceptance criterion 6, the required byte-stable/atomic failure behavior, and the prohibition on weakening atomic persistence.
findings.requiredRemediation: Implement an interruption-safe two-record adoption protocol that either exposes both successor records or preserves/restores both predecessor records across process termination, and make every reader fail closed on or deterministically recover any prepared/partial combination. Bind the transaction to the exact expected backlog/state bytes and approved evidence commit, fsync the required files/directories on Windows as appropriate, and add child-process abrupt-termination tests at every persistence boundary plus stale/concurrent failure tests proving byte-stable predecessor state or a fully consistent successor. Preserve this R01 finding append-only and close it only with fresh R02 evidence from a strict-descendant candidate.
